name: Mette Frederiksen
party: Socialdemokratiet (S, Social Democrats) — Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D) in the European Parliament
bio: Mette Frederiksen, born in Aalborg in 1977 and a graduate of Aalborg University and the University of Copenhagen, has been Prime Minister of Denmark since 27 June 2019 and leader of the Social Democrats (Socialdemokratiet) since 2015; she was 41 when she took office, the youngest Danish prime minister to date. A member of the Folketing since 2001, she was Minister for Employment (2011–2014) and Minister of Justice (2014–2015) under Helle Thorning-Schmidt. Her first government (2019–2022), a Social Democratic minority cabinet backed by the red-bloc parties, passed a binding Climate Act and a right to early retirement and handled the COVID-19 pandemic, including the November 2020 order to cull all farmed mink, which a commission of inquiry later found had no legal basis and which led to a formal parliamentary reprimand in July 2022. After the 2022 election she formed a cross-bloc coalition with Venstre and the Moderates (2022–2026) that abolished the Store Bededag public holiday to fund defence, reformed income tax and extended conscription to women; her governments have combined a restrictive asylum and immigration policy with welfare measures and have strongly supported Ukraine. During the 2025–2026 dispute over US President Donald Trump's calls to acquire Greenland she insisted on the Kingdom's sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination; on 22 September 2026 she signed a Greenland–Denmark–US defence agreement in New York, which still needs parliamentary approval. In the snap election of 24 March 2026 the Social Democrats stayed the largest party but fell to 21.8% and 38 seats, their weakest result since 1903; after ten weeks as caretaker she formed, on 3 June 2026, a four-party minority government (Social Democrats, Green Left/SF, Moderates and Social Liberals) holding 82 of the 179 seats, her third cabinet, as of October 2026.
